title: Finance & Legal: Integrated Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and RevRec Guidance (2026 Q2)
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Operational guidance for Redwood Inference finance and legal teams that standardizes budgeting & forecasting cadence, procurement and contract intake procedures, approval thresholds, and revenue recognition / billing policies for FY2026. Designed for finance, legal, procurement, and engineering stakeholders who create or approve spend and contracts.
content:
Overview

This document consolidates our FY2026 Q2 guidance for: budgeting and forecasting cadence; procurement and contract intake processes; approval thresholds and required artifacts; and revenue recognition (RevRec) and billing policy reminders. It is intended to reduce review friction, improve auditability, and ensure consistent RevRec treatment across hosted, dedicated, and private product lines.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood legal entities and product lines (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Covers capital vs. expense classification for platform spend, standard contract intake, procurement for cloud/GPU capacity, third-party SaaS, and professional services.
- Includes RevRec rules for usage-based hosted billing, committed capacity contracts, and multi-element arrangements (support, professional services, onboarding).

Key contacts and ownership

- Finance (Budget Owner): Miguel Torres, Head of FP&A — owns forecast consolidation, variance analysis, and reporting.
- Legal (Contract Owner): Sofia Nguyen, Senior Counsel — owns contract terms, NDAs, SOWs, and signature authority matrix reviews.
- Procurement/Ops: Liam O'Connor, Procurement Lead — owns purchase order issuance and vendor onboarding.
- Product/Engineering Requestor: requestor listed on intake form; owns technical acceptance criteria.

Budgeting & Forecasting cadence

1) Annual planning (Oct-Nov): owners submit FY+1 baseline requests using the Budget Template (see Appendix A). Baseline includes headcount, cloud/GPU capacity, and one-time capital items.
2) Rolling quarterly forecasts (RRF) — cadence and responsibilities:
   - Week 1 (of each quarter): FP&A issues forecast workbook template and prior quarter variance.
   - Week 2: Cost center owners update line-items, with notes for material variances (>10% or $100k).
   - Week 3: Finance consolidates and runs sensitivity scenarios (currency, spot GPU price +/- 20%).
   - Week 4: Executive review and forecast sign-off.
3) Scenario modeling: owners should maintain a 'p50' and 'p90' scenario for capacity-driven costs (GPU hours, storage, egress).

Forecast inputs and models

- Revenue drivers: hosted API monthly active customers (MAU), committed slots for Dedicated, and private deployment license fees.
- Cost drivers: GPU hours (by instance family), inference token volume (for third-party cost passthrough), and SRE/ops support FTE allocation.
- Assumptions must be documented in a single sheet: pricing assumptions, FX rates, and model version.

Approval thresholds and artifacts (table)

Approval thresholds (apply to procurement and contract signing):

- Individual contributor PO (pre-approval): <= $5k — department lead approves.
- Manager approval: $5k < amount <= $50k — department manager approvals + Procurement intake form.
- Director approval: $50k < amount <= $250k — Director + Procurement + Legal (if contract).
- VP approval: $250k < amount <= $1M — VP finance + Legal + Procurement review.
- Executive / CFO approval: > $1M — CFO approval required; Legal and Finance must pre-clear.

Required artifacts per approval level:

- All purchases: completed Procurement Intake Form, business justification, expected GL codes.
- Contracts (> $5k): draft SOW or Master Services Agreement (MSA), vendor W9 / company registration, security questionnaire if handling customer data.
- > $250k: commercial terms summary (term, termination, SLAs, liability cap), and RevRec classification recommendation from FP&A.

Procurement & contract intake process (step-by-step)

1) Requestor completes Procurement Intake Form (Confluence form link) with: vendor name, scope, estimated spend, GL codes, duration, and product owner acceptance criteria.
2) Procurement triage (Liam O'Connor): validate vendor, confirm onboarding checklist, and assign PO or Contract Owner.
3) Legal review (Sofia Nguyen): analyze commercial terms, IP, data protection, export controls, and standard redlines.
4) Finance review (Miguel Torres): confirm budget availability, suggested accounting treatment (capex vs opex), and RevRec guidance for customer-facing arrangements.
5) Signature & PO issuance: signatory per approval thresholds issues signature; Procurement issues PO or contract execution record.

Contract intake checklist (required attachments)

- Fully executed NDA (if needed)
- Draft MSA or SOW with: term dates, fees, invoicing schedule, payment terms, termination and refund clauses
- Vendor TIN/W9 or equivalent entity verification
- Security & privacy questionnaire results or SOC/ISO attestation where applicable
- Proof of insurance where required
- Cost breakdown for multi-element arrangements (e.g., implementation + ongoing service)

Procurement templates and examples

- Example PO line-item structure (text table):
  | GL_Code | Description | Qty | Unit Price | Total | Owner |
  | 6100    | GPU Spot Hours | 1 | $120,000 | $120,000 | Eng SRE |

- Example procurement intake JSON (for automation team — place as a code block):
  {
    "vendor": "Example GPU Provider",
    "estimated_annual_spend": "120000",
    "cost_center": "eng-infra",
    "justification": "Additional Reserved Capacity for Dedicated customers",
    "terms": "12 months, net 30",
    "security_attestation": "SOC2 Type 2 on file"
  }

Revenue recognition & billing policy (summary)

Principles
- Revenue is recognized when (a) the performance obligations are satisfied and (b) collectability is probable.
- For usage-based hosted API, revenue is recognized as the service is delivered (over time) with measurement based on recorded usage metrics.
- For committed/dedicated capacity contracts with upfront or recurring fees: allocate transaction price to performance obligations (hosting, support, onboarding). Upfront implementation fees are recognized as follows: if the implementation service is distinct, recognize when delivered; if not distinct, defer and recognize over the hosting term.

Common contract patterns and RevRec treatment

1) Hosted API (usage-based, invoiced monthly): recognize revenue monthly as usage occurs.
2) Dedicated (committed capacity, recurring monthly/quarterly): allocate to hosting (over time) and any separate professional services. If the customer prepays a year, recognize hosting revenue ratably each month; recognize professional services when delivered.
3) Private deployment (license + installation + support): license revenue recognized per the license agreement (may be upfront if perpetual license and no further obligations) and support recognized ratably. Installation and customization are evaluated for distinctness.

Billing & invoicing operations

- Billing cadence: monthly for hosted usage customers; net terms per contract (standard net 30).
- Invoice content: customer name, contract/PO reference, billing period, line-item usage detail, taxes, and payment instructions.
- Dispute & dispute hold: disputes must be raised within 30 days of invoice; disputed amounts can be placed on hold per the dispute matrix.

Tax and compliance notes

- Sales tax/VAT: Billing team applies tax per customer region; finance works with tax advisors for complex jurisdictions.
- Withholding taxes: For cross-border services, Legal and Finance coordinate on contract language and invoicing to manage withholding obligations.

Exception handling and escalation

- Exceptions that bypass standard thresholds require a documented business case, sign-off from Requestor manager, Procurement lead, Legal, and VP Finance.
- Emergency procurement (e.g., critical capacity purchase) must be documented in post-facto review within 7 business days.

Auditability & record retention

- All executed contracts and procurement artifacts are stored in the Contracts repository (DocStore link) with retention of at least 7 years for material contracts.
- PO issuance logs and invoice archives retained per finance record retention policy.

Appendix A — Budget template (high-level fields)

- Department / Cost center
- Line item description
- Annual amount (USD)
- Capital vs. Operating classification
- Vendor (if known)
- Accountable owner (name, email)
- Assumptions / notes

Appendix B — Sample RevRec decision matrix (text)

- Is service delivered over time? -> Yes -> Recognize over time.
- Is implementation distinct from hosting? -> Yes -> Recognize implementation when delivered. -> No -> Defer implementation revenue and recognize over hosting term.

Appendix C — Links and related pages

- Contracts playbook: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contracts-procurement-playbook-2026.json
- RevRec policy: /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/revenue-recognition-billing-policy-2026.json
- Procurement Intake Form: /confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/procurement-intake-form (internal form link)

Questions and feedback

For questions about budgeting or RevRec treatment, contact Miguel Torres (FP&A). For contract or legal questions, contact Sofia Nguyen (Legal). For procurement intake or supplier onboarding, contact Liam O'Connor (Procurement).
